conviction_note: The findings roughly cancel (impact_sum +0.5). Negatives: Helen of Troy said on 8 Oct that insulated beverageware is saturated and turning promotional, YETI discounted 139 of 202 Amazon listings for Prime Big Deal Days, and Traeger reported Asian shipments slipping from Q3 into Q4. Positives: tariff rates sit below the ~20% YETI guided on, 11% of shares are short at 7.3 days to cover, and the stock fell 8.8% in the five days into the print. This name sold off 10.6% on its last beat-and-raise and the 25-delta skew pays for downside, so p_up is 49 against an abs move of 9.0 (above the 8.36 implied, because the last two prints moved 10.6 and 6.2 and the holiday guide is at stake). The scaled number is about -0.2 and the sum +0.5: same tiny size, opposite sign, and neither is a call.
bar: Revenue: $523.0M average of 16 analysts (range $519-532M) on Yahoo https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/YETI/analysis/ and $522.5M on Earnings Whispers; the two agree, and the company guide lands in the same place (FY +7-8%, growth 'relatively consistent throughout the rest of the year', i.e. Q3 about $522-527M against $487.8M a year ago). Adj EPS: $0.84 average of 17 (range $0.72-0.89) on Yahoo and $0.83 on Benzinga, against $0.73-0.74 on TipRanks/Earnings Whispers, so the EPS bar is partly disputed. The guide implies about $0.85-0.88: H2 adj operating margin +280bp YoY on Q3'25's 13.7%, 24% tax, about 73.5M diluted shares (72.99M outstanding at 6 Aug). FY adj EPS consensus is $2.97 against a $2.94-3.00 guide. So the bar sits at the company guide, and a reported-quarter beat is not where the move comes from.
positioning_check: Short interest (Equibles, FINRA settlements): 8.12M shares, 11.1% of 72.99M shares outstanding, 7.29 days to cover at 2026-10-30, up from 7.07M / 4.81 days at 2026-10-15 (+15% in two weeks) https://equibles.com/stocks/yeti/shortinterest . So the short is moderately crowded and rising into the print. Options: 25d skew +4.4 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI ratio 2.82, event-implied move 8.36%, ATM spread 28% of mid. Tape: 5d -8.81% and 20d +8.79%. The stock ran from about $43 in late October to about $49 on 5 Nov, then gave it back (Fox Business quote: -4.21% to $46.94 on 6 Nov), and no cause turned up. FMR rose from 5.3% to 7.7% at 30 Sep (13G/A, 5 Nov). Reinhart Partners filed a new 13G at 5.1%.

findings.finding: Helen of Troy (Hydro Flask), reporting 8 Oct 2026 after YETI last spoke, said 'the beverage wear category as a whole is a little bit saturated, and we see that environment becoming promotional', that 'some inventory correction [is] needed in the channel in the beverage category', and that 'Hydro Flask is the driver of the Home & Outdoor revision to our outlook for revenue' in H2. That is a direct-competitor read against YETI Drinkware (about 50% of sales; +2% in Q2, US flat), where YETI guided mid-single-digit FY growth implying H2 acceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Drinkware is the line YETI trades on. On 2026-08-13 an EPS beat ($0.67 vs $0.55) plus a guide raise still fell 10.56%, on US Drinkware flat and the disclosed 600bp US Drinkware drag (sgbonline). On 2026-02-19 a weak guide moved it -4.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: It has been public for a month, but YETI's own H2 Drinkware guide (mid-single-digit FY, needing acceleration from +2%) has not been revisited since 13 Aug, and the 17 Sep Investor Day reiterated it. FY consensus revenue of $2.01B still sits at the guide. If the market had marked YETI down for the category, FY revenue estimates would have moved below $2.00B and Q3 EPS revisions would show more than 1 down in 7 days. Partly priced: the put skew and the 5d -8.8% may already hold it.
findings.independence: YETI's own Q2 call (https://s22.q4cdn.com/322452763/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/YETI-2Q26-Earnings-Transcript.pdf) described 'continued Drinkware market pressure and competition', and HELE's 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000916789/000091678926000137/fy27_q2xex-991.htm) shows Home & Outdoor +9.2% in Q2, so the weakness is a forward (H2) call, not a realised quarter. Net of the rest of the company: Coolers & Equipment (+16% in Q2) and International (+19%) are about half of sales and have to carry the guide.

findings.finding: During Amazon Prime Big Deal Days (6-7 Oct 2026, inside fiscal Q4), 139 of YETI's 202 Amazon listings were marked down, by 8% to 42% (Rambler 14oz mug $22 vs $38; Roadie 48 down $102). That is promotional breadth on YETI's largest marketplace channel at the start of the holiday quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 call credited 'pricing discipline' and lower promotion for 110bp of operational gross-margin gain; a promotional reversal would hit Q4 margin, where management guided H2 operating margin +280bp YoY with Q4 above that. No prior print isolates promotions.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates this, and I have no year-ago comparison; YETI has run Prime-day discounts before (Tom's Guide coverage in 2024/2025). If it were read as a new promotional stance, analysts would be cutting Q4 gross-margin estimates, and FY EPS consensus ($2.97) still sits at the guide midpoint.
findings.independence: Same promotional theme as Helen of Troy's 'environment becoming promotional' (finding 1, a different source). It is a proxy: whether these were funded markdowns or Amazon-funded, and how they compare to last October, is unknown.

findings.finding: YETI's FY26 guide 'assumes tariff rates returning to approximately 20% beginning in September', which the CFO called 'conservative'. The tariff in force since 24 Jul 2026 is the Section 301 forced-labor action at 13% for Vietnam, China, Philippines and Thailand and 10% for Mexico, Malaysia and India, with no scheduled increase. The excess-capacity Section 301 case was still open as of early November. So H2 landed tariff cost is running below the guide's assumption, which is room for a gross-margin beat or a Q4/FY guide raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: guide raised (EPS $2.94-3.00 from $2.83-2.89) partly on tariffs, and the stock fell 10.56% because Drinkware dominated. Q1 2026: EPS guide raised and the stock rose 6.16%. Q3 2025: the tariff headwind beat and the stock rose 5.21%. Tariff-driven margin upside has been bought only when Drinkware did not dominate.
findings.why_not_priced: The rates were public before the 13 Aug guide, so analysts know the gap. But FY consensus EPS of $2.97 sits inside the $2.94-3.00 guide rather than above it, so the street has not booked the difference between ~13% and ~20%. With moving-average inventory costing, the gap shows in Q4 more than Q3, so it reaches this print through the guide, not the quarter. If it were priced, FY estimates would sit above the top of the guide, and the skew would not be paying for downside.
findings.independence: YETI Q2 call transcript (https://s22.q4cdn.com/322452763/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/YETI-2Q26-Earnings-Transcript.pdf, p.10 and p.14): the 20%-from-September assumption, plus the CFO's 'just being conservative' given 'remaining investigations'. Counterweight in the same transcript: commodity, freight and FX inflation 'have gotten worse', and OpEx growth was raised to 6-8%. Size is net of that.

findings.finding: Guide arithmetic puts Q3 at about $522-527M revenue and about $0.85-0.88 adj EPS: FY sales +7-8% with growth 'relatively consistent throughout the rest of the year'; H2 adj operating margin +280bp YoY (Q4 slightly more) on Q3'25's 13.7%; about 73.5M diluted shares against 72.99M outstanding at 6 Aug. That sits at or a hair above the $523M / $0.84 consensus, so the reported quarter is pre-set by the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats have not been paid: +$0.12-0.13 vs consensus in Q2 2026 went with -10.56%, and an EPS decline in Q1 2026 went with +6.16%. The stock trades on Drinkware and the guide, not the EPS line.
findings.why_not_priced: It mostly is: consensus already sits at the guide. What may be unpriced is the share count, since the 6 Aug cover count (72.99M) is below the 75.8M Q2 weighted figure, but analysts can read the cover page. If the street were below this arithmetic, Q3 EPS consensus would not have drifted only from $0.87 to $0.84 over 90 days.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 base from the company's 3Q25 release (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35947313/yeti-reports-third-quarter-2025-results): adj op margin 13.7%, adj EPS $0.61. Share count from the 10-Q cover (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1670592/000167059226000040/yeti-20260704.htm). Same company documents as finding 3 and finding 8, but a different line.

findings.finding: Traeger, reporting 4 Nov 2026, said Q3 revenue fell 40% partly because shipments moved into Q4, citing 'container constraints amplified by a typhoon in Asia'. That flags inbound Asian freight disruption in YETI's fiscal Q3 (ended about 3 Oct), which could shift some wholesale sell-in out of Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Wholesale timing has moved YETI quarters before: Q1 2026 wholesale +19% offset corporate sales, and Canada sell-in was soft in Q2. No YETI print has been explained by freight timing.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out a week before the print, and nobody has tied it to YETI. YETI said on 13 Aug that its inventory was 'the healthiest position we've had in quite some time' ($359M, +5%) and its supply chain was diversified, which limits the transmission. If priced, Q3 revenue estimates would have slipped from $523M; the range low is still $519M.
findings.independence: Proxy only. YETI's Q2 call mentioned 'shipping delays across certain Asia trade lanes' (same transcript as findings 3 and 4). No direct YETI confirmation for Q3.

findings.finding: Short interest is 11.1% of shares outstanding (8.12M) at 7.29 days to cover on the 30 Oct settlement, up 15% from 7.07M / 4.81 days on 15 Oct. The stock fell 8.81% over the five sessions into the print, and puts are bid (skew +4.4, put/call OI 2.82). The book is leaning short into a release whose reported quarter is pre-set by the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a 44% run in the months following the Q3 2025 print (Motley Fool, Jan 2026), the stock rose 5.21% on Q3 2025 and 6.16% on Q1 2026 when Drinkware did not disappoint. Short squeezes are not documented for YETI.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, so this is about asymmetry, not information. With 7.3 days to cover and shorts added in late October, a clean Drinkware line or a raised Q4 tariff margin forces covering. If the short had already been covered, days to cover would have fallen and the 5d move would not be -8.8%.
findings.independence: Baseline skew +4.4 and 5d run-up -8.81% (sealed baseline file). Days-to-cover figures differ across vendors (Stocktitan shows 5.3, undated).

findings.finding: FMR (Fidelity) raised its YETI holding from 3.99M shares (5.3%, at 30 Jun) to 5.63M shares (7.7%, at 30 Sep), per the 13G/A filed 5 Nov 2026. A large long holder added about 1.6M shares during the quarter being reported.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; ownership filings have not been tied to YETI's prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and says nothing about the quarter. It is filed only because it bears on who holds the stock into the print (a sticky long base against a rising short). If it mattered, it would have moved the stock on 5 Nov, and the stock fell on 6 Nov.
findings.independence: Prior FMR 13G https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1670592/000031506626002200/primary_doc.xml (5.3% at 30 Jun). Reinhart Partners also filed a new 13G at 5.1% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1670592/000108029826000013/primary_doc.xml, 13 Oct).

findings.finding: YETI said the three US Drinkware SKUs causing a roughly 600bp drag on 2026 US Drinkware growth 'will largely complete their lap by year-end, resetting the base as we head into 2027'. The Q3 call is the first chance to give an early 2027 Drinkware read off a clean base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When this drag was disclosed (13 Aug 2026) the stock fell 10.56%. YETI does not formally guide the next year until the Q4 print in February.
findings.why_not_priced: It is company-stated and public, and management confirmed it was already in the FY guide. What could move the stock is call colour on 2027, which no estimate carries yet. Mostly priced.
findings.independence: Same transcript as findings 3 and 4; set against finding 1 (Helen of Troy says the category is still saturated), which argues the lap may not produce a clean 2027 re-base.

outside_window.finding: USTR's Section 301 excess-capacity investigation into 16 economies (including China and Vietnam), opened 11 Mar 2026, had produced no tariff as of early November. Its statutory deadline is 11 Mar 2027, so any new tariff on YETI's source countries would land after the window, though management may comment on it.

baseline_tension: The negatives (Helen of Troy category read, Amazon markdowns, Traeger freight) agree with the +4.4 put skew and the 5d -8.8% slide, so they are probably partly priced. The tariff gap and the rising 11%-of-shares short cut against the skew. Net, the evidence does not beat the baseline, and p_up sits at 49.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, 11% at 7.3 days to cover): Helen of Troy category negative shrunk from -1.0 to -0.8; Traeger freight proxy from -0.3 to -0.2.

Lesson 7 (sign against the +4.4 skew): tariff-gap positive shrunk from +1.0 to +0.8, with the stated reason the market may be wrong (FY consensus sits inside a guide built on a 20% tariff that is running about 13%).
Lessons 1 and 6 (beats sold; finding inside the company guide): guide-arithmetic reported-quarter finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
Lesson 9: the Drinkware negative is already sized net of Coolers & Equipment (+16%) and International (+19%); no further change.
The two changes offset, so impact_sum stays at +0.5; p_up (49) and abs_move (9.0) unchanged.
